description: A change to the review loop entrypoint made it overlay a git identity on the process environment. It passed CI and review because both run the test suite in a plain environment where the overlay is absent. The overlay only matters when the resolver runs the pre-push suite as a child of the review loop, where two deterministic tests then failed and halted three flows.
goal: Add a contract test that builds the environment the review loop hands to its child processes, runs a child pytest over the two canary tests (the executor-identity salvage test in test_executor_run_salvage.py and the history test in test_flow_repo_templates.py) under that environment, and requires the child to pass; the test fails when the review loop environment leaks identity variables that those tests do not tolerate. The test is hermetic, needs no network and finishes within the unit time budget. Only a new test file is added; no source file changes. Code is self-explaining: names state the intent; no docstrings and no comments in any language except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: Plain-environment CI cannot see a regression that only appears in a child process of the review loop. A contract test over the canary tests catches the class of change before it halts flows.
acceptance_criteria: The new test runs a child pytest over the two canary tests with the review loop's child environment and passes on current main.
Reverting the identity fix makes the new test fail.
The test is hermetic, runs under uv run pytest, and adds no docstring or comment other than '# why:'.
No file other than the new test file changes.
